summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia s/p transplant and chronic graft-versus-host disease, was admitted after experiencing transient aphasic episodes described as 'fits.' Workup included CT and MRI of the head, which ruled out stroke, hemorrhage, or mass. Respiratory testing was negative for viral infection, and chest imaging showed stable inflammatory changes without pneumonia. He was found to have B12 deficiency, contributing to neurological symptoms, and was started on supplementation. His episodes were determined to be a mix of neurological and emotional factors, leading to a diagnosis of predominant disturbance of emotions, possibly exacerbated by steroid use. He also had secondary diabetes, hypercholesterolemia, cardiomyopathy, and esophageal reflux, all managed during admission. He improved clinically, remained stable, and was discharged with follow-up arranged in hematology, neurology, and psychiatry.
problems: Acute myeloid leukemia, without mention of having achieved remission
Secondary diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, not stated as uncontrolled, or unspecified
Adrenal cortical steroids causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
